items.title: Federal Court judge criticises Najib's lawyers over late adjournment bid
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A Federal Court judge today criticised Datuk Seri Najib Razak's lawyers for making a last-minute attempt to postpone proceedings in his RM1.9 million civil suit against former attorney-general Tan Sri Tommy Thomas. Justice Datuk Azimah Omar said Najib's legal team should have filed the application for an adjournment as soon as they knew he was on medical leave, to avoid wasting the court's time as judges had spent hours preparing for the case. Court of Appeal president Datuk Abu Bakar Jais and Federal Court judge Datuk Azmi Ariffin formed the majority.

items.title: RCI pushes for new Haj Fund dept to safeguard Tabung Haji’s future as deposits approach RM100b
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) has recommended the establishment of a dedicated department known as the Haj Fund under TH to manage depositors’ funds, with oversight by the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) to enhance investment management professionalism. The RCI said the move would allow TH to retain its investment management functions rather than be placed under a separate subsidiary. The TH Board would appoint senior officers, including the chief investment officer, who would be supervised by the SC.

items.title: APHR: Myanmar not safe for Rohingya return
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asean Parliamentarians for Human Rights (APHR) co-chair Charles Santiago has questioned the plan to repatriate 5,000 Rohingya refugees to Myanmar. "Malaysia cannot, in good conscience, celebrate the return of 5,000 Rohingya to Myanmar without first answering one fundamental question: return them to what?" The concern follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's announcement on Wednesday that Myanmar has agreed to take back 5,000 Rohingya currently in Malaysia, as part of a wider regional repatriation effort involving 300,000 refugees in Bangladesh.

items.title: 52 smuggled durian saplings seized, man arrested
items.summary: GOF Southeast Brigade commander Senior Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Radzi Hussain said the seizure was made by its Seventh Battalion, assisted by the Kelantan Agriculture Department. He said the team intercepted a pickup truck along Jalan Jubakar in Kampung Kaki Itek at 3.45pm after finding it transporting the saplings without valid documentation. "After inspecting the vehicle, the team uncovered 52 durian saplings suspected of carrying plant pests.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia's Q2 net profit jumps 26pct, IPO target raised
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia Bhd's net profit jumped 25.9 per cent to RM71.78 million in the second quarter ended June 30 2026 from RM57.06 million a year earlier. Bursa Malaysia's revenue climbed 22.3 per cent to RM210.97 million from RM172.58 million. The stronger performance lifted Bursa Malaysia's first-half net profit 15.2 per cent to RM144.61 million from RM125.48 million, with revenue rising 19.1 per cent to RM425.04 million.

items.title: Iran's IRGC says Strait of Hormuz cannot reopen while US 'threats' continue
items.summary: TEHERAN, (Iran): Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said Thursday that the Strait of Hormuz cannot be reopened as long as US threats and interference in regional maritime traffic continue, Anadolu Ajansi reported. "The Strait of Hormuz cannot be reopened as long as the bluster and threats of US officials and their interference in maritime movements in the region continue," the IRGC said in a statement. The IRGC claimed that two oil tankers, "at the instigation of US aircraft," attempted overnight to transit through what it described as an "unsafe route" south of the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Indonesia weather agency warns El Nino to last through early 2027
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia recorded a sharp increase in potential fire zones in July as El Nino conditions intensified across the country, the head of the country's weather agency said on Thursday, adding that the weather system was expected to last into early 2027. More than 5,000 hotspots were detected as of July 29, a sharp increase compared to previous El Niño years in 2015, 2019 and 2023, agency official Ardhasena Sopaheluwakan said in an online briefing. There were 1,366 locations with dry spells lasting 21-30 days, 943 locations with 31-60 rainless days, and 70 locations where dry conditions persisted for more than 60 days.

items.title: Abdul Azeez says ready to face fresh probe over Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: JELEBU, July 30 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim said he is prepared to be investigated again if necessary following allegations of misconduct raised in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report, according to Sinar Harian. Abdul Azeez said the 204-page RCI report had been completed at the end of 2022 and tabled at several Cabinet meetings. Abdul Azeez said he had previously appealed to then prime minister Dr Mahathir, then deputy prime minister Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail and former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Seri Mujahid Yusof Rawa to establish an RCI into the matter.

items.title: Four escaped Puspen inmates rearrested in Sungai Siput
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Anti-Drugs Agency (Nada) has confirmed that four inmates who escaped from the Perlop Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) in Perak on July 24 have been rearrested. Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said all four were detained in the Sungai Siput district with the assistance of police and local villagers. "The viral message is false as all four inmates escaped and remained within the Sungai Siput district before they were rearrested," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Amendments to Tabung Haji Act in the works following RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Stakeholder engagement sessions on proposed amendments to the Tabung Haji Act 1995 have been held following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the feedback and views gathered would be taken into account to ensure the proposed amendments were appropriate and effective. He said the proposed amendments were among the RCI's 25 recommendations to strengthen Tabung Haji, with about 75 per cent of the recommendations already implemented.

items.title: Are Malaysia’s small traders ready for Asean’s digital economy? Yes, even fried banana sellers use QR codes, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Malaysia's micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) are well positioned to tap Asean's 680-million-consumer market under the proposed Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA), supported by their high level of digital adoption, Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said. He said harmonising digital regulatory frameworks would reduce market fragmentation, creating a more efficient, cost-effective and globally competitive Asean digital economic bloc. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin is confident that Malaysia’s micro, small and medium enterprises are ready for Asean’s cross-border digital trade.

items.title: South Korea's women web sleuths fight AI deepfake porn
items.summary: UNDER banners emblazoned "Solidarity" and "We stand together with victims", a group of South Korean women digital detectives dredges the internet for a scourge of illegal AI-enabled pornography. South Korea – home to the world's leading smartphone and memory chipmakers – takes huge national pride in its tech prowess. But the success story has a dark side: women suffer rampant "digital sex crimes", rights groups say.

items.title: Malaysia and Japan launch postgraduate programme for Palestine students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) and the Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) today signed an agreement to provide postgraduate education in engineering, science, and technology for Palestinian students under a six-year initiative starting October this year. Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the rebuilding of Palestine must extend beyond restoring physical infrastructure to focus on developing human capital through higher education. Zambry said education was key to producing the engineers, researchers, educators, planners, and leaders needed to support Palestine's long-term recovery.

items.title: Man faces murder charges over fatal Teluk Intan crash
items.summary: TELUK INTAN: A 28-year-old man was charged in the magistrate's court here today with four offences, including the murder of two schoolgirls in a crash near a secondary school on Sunday. Alex Robert, a private sector employee in Singapore, was charged with murdering Nur Dania Arissa Salim, 17, and Nur Atikah Abdullah, 16, near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Seri Setia on Jalan Padang Tembak at 6.35pm on July 26. No plea was recorded on the two murder charges as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.

items.title: Woman pleads not guilty to alleged fake payment receipt charge
items.summary: KUANTAN: A housewife has claimed trial at the Magistrate's Court here today to a charge of allegedly submitting a fake payment receipt for RM8,998. Nurwahidah Khamirrudin, 35, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read before magistrate Tuan Ruzuaini Tuan Lah. The mother of two was accused of deceiving a 19-year-old woman by submitting a false payment transaction receipt.

items.title: 8-year-old struggles to comprehend loss of parents, brother in Hulu Langat crash
items.summary: KAJANG: The 8-year-old son of a couple killed in a crash in Hulu Langat yesterday is struggling to come to terms with the loss of his parents and three-year-old brother. Hafifi is survived by his two sons, aged eight and 10. Rahmat said the family would pursue insurance claims to help support Hafifi's two surviving sons.

items.title: RM1,000 subsidy and a new centre: How Malaysia is stepping up support for kids with autism as registrations rise
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — About 93,000 of the 850,000 persons with disabilities (PwDs) registered with the Department of Social Welfare (JKM) as of June this year are those with autism, the Dewan Negara was told today. Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said the increase in registrations had prompted the government to enhance various initiatives on early intervention, education and skills training for the group. “Recently, the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) established an Autism Service Centre in Bangi with the primary objective of providing a one-stop centre offering quality, affordable and easily accessible services,” she said when replying to a question from Senator Dr A. Lingeshwaran.

items.title: Agriculture Ministry says Malaysia imports too much ginger, mangoes, rice and fresh milk — here’s what’s changing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The Ministry of Agriculture and Food Security (KPKM) is focusing on increasing the production of agri-food commodities with low Self-Sufficiency Ratio (SSR) levels to reduce the country’s dependence on food imports. Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Chan Foong Hin said commodities that still require attention include ginger, with an SSR of 15.5 per cent, mangoes (20 per cent), rice (about 52 per cent) and fresh milk (66.7 per cent). Meanwhile, in response to concerns over food supply to rural areas in Sabah and Sarawak, Chan said KPKM is working with PLANMalaysia to develop the National Food Source Area Land Use Planning Master Plan to safeguard food production areas.

items.title: 8 detained in Kota Baru operation following begging complaints
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Eight people, including a nine-year-old girl, were picked up in a joint enforcement operation last night targeting homeless individuals and street beggars in Kota Baru. Kelantan Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the operation was jointly carried out with the Kota Baru Municipal Council, the Immigration Department and the police. He said the operation, led by council enforcement division chief Mohamad Ali, targeted homeless individuals and street beggars around Kota Baru, including areas near banks, Dataran Muhammadi and Dataran Bandaraya.

items.title: Mother relieved as drink-driving suspect faces murder charge
items.summary: KLANG: The mother of food delivery rider Zulfiqar Zamir Amirul Nizam said she felt a sense of relief after the man accused of fatally crashing into her son was charged with murder. Hamidah Othman, 51, said the prosecution made the right decision after Zulfiqar died on May 25, 13 days after the alleged drink-driving crash. My son died senselessly," she said.

items.title: Money laundering charges: Former GISB chief, three ex-accountants to learn fate of representations on Oct 3
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, July 30 — The Sessions Court today fixed Oct 3 to decide on representations submitted by former GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) chief executive officer Nasiruddin Mohd Ali and three former company accountants in relation to 331 money laundering charges involving more than RM38.1 million. The four accused are Nasiruddin, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, who faces 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, who faces 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, who faces 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million. Counsel Muhammad Zaim Rosli appeared for Nasiruddin, Asmat @ Asmanira and Mohd Khushairi.

items.title: Penang's Sungai Nibong TOD aims to reduce car dependency
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Limiting car dependency through efficient public transport, pedestrian-friendly design and parking controls will be key to the success of the proposed Sungai Nibong transit-oriented development (TOD). Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said concerns over worsening congestion along Jalan Sultan Azlan Shah were understandable given the high-density development proposed for the area. However, he said the TOD concept was specifically designed to reduce reliance on private vehicles by integrating residential, commercial and recreational developments with high-capacity public transport.

items.title: Govt to speed up remaining Tabung Haji reform recommendations, says Islamic Affairs minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The government will expedite the implementation of the remaining 25 per cent of recommendations by the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), taking into account current realities and other relevant considerations, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan. On the recommendation to restructure TH’s governance, he said he was open to considering the proposal, including separating responsibilities for financial, fund and investment management under the Finance Minister. Zulkifli said the recommendation to limit the scope of the Religious Affairs Minister’s authority to haj management was among the suggestions contained in the RCI report published yesterday.

items.title: CAP calls for immediate vape ban, says RM369mil health cost a waste
items.summary: CAP senior education officer NV Subbarow urged the government to stop delaying action and implement a total ban to protect public health. "The RM369 million health cost is a waste. Go for a total vape ban and save the millions," he said today.

items.title: Draft Sungai Nibong TOD master plan to be finalised by October
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The draft master plan for the Sungai Nibong transit-oriented development (TOD) is expected to be finalised by October, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said today. He said the state government is currently conducting stakeholder engagement sessions before finalising the conceptual master plan, with implementation expected to span between 10 and 15 years. Penang is aiming to transform Sungai Nibong into the state's first inclusive TOD, setting a benchmark for future rail-linked urban development.

items.title: Trump's attorney general pick hits snag as key senator withholds support
items.summary: WASHINGTON: Todd Blanche's bid for Senate confirmation as US attorney general faced a potential setback on Wednesday when Republican Senator John Cornyn cited unresolved concerns over a controversial US$1.8 billion fund tied to Trump allies. Cornyn's opposition could prove decisive. "I'm not prepared to vote yes" on Blanche's nomination, Cornyn told reporters.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia slightly lower at midday amid geopolitical tensions, fed rate hold
items.summary: Among heavyweights, Tenaga Nasional eased four sen to RM14.56, CIMB shed one sen to RM7.80, and Public Bank dropped two sen to RM5.13. Of the active stocks, Zetrix AI slid one sen to 69.5 sen, VS Industry shed 1.5 sen to 22 sen, SNS Network Technology and HHRG slumped half-a-sen each to 53.5 sen and 13 sen, respectively. Sum Technology added 3.5 sen to 62 sen. As for the top gainers, Nestle advanced RM2.10 to RM98.88, Fraser & Neave Holdings jumped 36 sen to RM27.76, Kuala Lumpur Kepong rose 24 sen to RM21, Allianz Malaysia inched up 18 sen to RM21.18, and Westports Holdings climbed 15 sen to RM6.98.

items.title: Jalaluddin: 10 more Orang Asli villages to be gazetted if BN wins
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Another 10 Orang Asli villages in Negri Sembilan will be gazetted in the near future if Barisan Nasional m is given the mandate to form the state government in the Aug 1 state election. As a result, 58 of the state's 69 Orang Asli villages have already been gazetted. "The Orang Asli community needs the government's attention.

items.title: Govt to expedite remaining 25pct TH RCI recommendations, says Zulkifli
items.summary: Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the government was always open and ready to introduce changes while viewing the recommendations as an opportunity to further strengthen the institution. On the recommendation to restructure TH's governance, Zulkifli said he was open to considering the proposal, including separating responsibilities for financial, fund, and investment management under the finance minister. Zulkifli said MMKI, initiated by Co-opbank Pertama (CBP), also served as a reference platform for industry players involved in Islamic banking and finance.

items.title: BN to set up unit to monitor manifesto implementation, says Jalaluddin
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Barisan Nasional will ensure every pledge in its election manifesto is fully implemented through a dedicated monitoring unit. State Umno liaison committee chairman Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias said the manifesto implementation monitoring unit would be established immediately following the formation of the state government should the coalition secure a mandate in the Aug 1 election. He said the unit would track the progress of manifesto commitments through regular reports tabled during state executive council meetings.

items.title: Teach Adibah Amin's works to foster unity, says former judge
items.summary: The Universiti Malaya Pro-Chancellor said Adibah's writings remained highly relevant as Malaysia continued to navigate issues of race, religion, and social cohesion. Adibah Amin's 'As I Was Passing' belongs squarely to the latter," she said. Monash University Malaysia President and Pro Vice-Chancellor Prof Emeritus Datuk Dr Adeeba Kamarulzaman said the university was pleased to celebrate Adibah's work alongside Malaysia's rich literary and cultural heritage.

items.title: UMS, industry partner to develop sustainable battery-free lighting system in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, July 30 — A RM76,000 research project to develop a battery-free lighting system powered by thermal energy will be carried out in Sabah under the Industrial Collaboration Programme (ICP). The project, involving Universiti Malaysia Sabah (UMS) and Seni Gemilang Sdn Bhd, aims to advance sustainable energy research while developing a Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) learning module for schools in Sabah. The ICP is a government initiative led by the Ministry of Finance that uses selected government procurement projects to encourage technology adoption, research partnerships, innovation and talent development.

items.title: Low Danube levels force nuclear shutdown in Romania
items.summary: BUCHAREST: Romania will shut down its second nuclear reactor due to low water levels in the Danube, the energy ministry said Wednesday, days after the first was shut down for the same reason. The two reactors at the Cernavoda plant run by Romania's national nuclear energy company Nuclearelectrica rely on the waters of the Danube for cooling. Hungary has also reduced its nuclear output due to the river's low water levels.

items.title: OCBC Bank commits RM325mil to battery storage project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: OCBC Bank (Malaysia) Bhd has committed RM325 million to finance a utility-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) project under the government's Battery Energy Storage (MyBeST) programme. The financing will support a 100MW/400MWh BESS project by ERS Energy Sdn Bhd's unit ESS Bahau Sdn Bhd. OCBC Bank head of wholesale banking Jeffrey Teoh Nee Teik said the financing reflects the bank's commitment to supporting Malaysia's energy transition and critical energy infrastructure.

items.title: Putrajaya plans two new infertility clinics nationwide yearly to help low-income couples
items.summary: Deputy Minister Lim Hui Ying said the move aims to expand access to quality and affordable subfertility services, particularly to assist married couples from lower-income groups. She said fertility treatment services under the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN) are currently provided through four main zonal clinics, namely in Penang (Northern Zone), Kuala Lumpur (Central Zone), Johor Bahru (Southern Zone) and Kuching (East Malaysia Zone). Lim said the Buai Programme comprises two initiatives, namely subsidies for treatment fees, including medication and procedures, as well as advocacy programmes to increase participants’ understanding and knowledge.

items.title: Two 19-year-olds remanded over newborn's death
items.summary: District police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said the female suspect is currently receiving treatment at Enche' Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital. Earlier, Johor police chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police received a report at 1pm yesterday regarding a female student who was admitted to the hospital after allegedly giving birth. He said medical examinations confirmed that the student had delivered a baby, while another baby girl was found in her womb.

items.title: Private hospitals association re-elects Dr Kuljit Singh for fifth consecutive term
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh has been re-elected as president of the Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia (APHM) for a fifth consecutive term. Under his leadership, APHM has continued to engage with government policymakers and key healthcare stakeholders on issues affecting Malaysia's private healthcare sector. The newly elected council members are Dr Tan Hui Ling, Mohd Khairul Izzad Mohamed Shamsuddin, Poorani Ramachandran, Dr Seow Vei Kean, Dr Shuba Srinivasan, Tan Yew Aik and Stanley Lam.

items.title: One twin dead, one survives: Johor cops arrest college student and boyfriend over newborn's murder in Kluang toilet
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, July 30 — Police have arrested a 19-year-old college student and her boyfriend of the same age to assist in the investigation into the murder of a newborn baby girl found with multiple stab wounds at a rented house in Taman Setia Mutiara, Kluang, yesterday. Johor Police Chief Datuk Ab Rahaman Arsad said police received a report at 1 pm after the woman was admitted to Enche Besar Hajjah Khalsom Hospital following childbirth. The baby was subsequently delivered safely,” he told a press conference at the Johor Police Headquarters today.

items.title: Penang CM: Sungai Nibong TOD master plan expected to be finalised in October
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — The draft Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Master Plan for Sungai Nibong is expected to be finalised in October, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the state government is currently conducting engagement sessions with various stakeholders to gather feedback before finalising the master plan. Chow said the implementation phase would be the challenging part and was projected to take between 10 and 15 years.

items.title: Penang to decide on temporary venue for Pesta Pulau Pinang within weeks
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government will decide within weeks whether Pesta Pulau Pinang will be held at a temporary venue during the redevelopment of the Sungai Nibong site. He said the state government was considering several options before making a final decision. Elaborating, Chow said the first option was not to hold Pesta Pulau Pinang during the construction period.

items.title: Verify all state-owned land deals first, Pahang tells public after fraud case in Bentong
items.summary: KUANTAN, July 30 — The Pahang government has uncovered a land application fraud syndicate in the Bentong district involving state-owned land. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the syndicate offered land alienation services by asking members of the public to make payments and sign documents before the process was carried out. “I would like to emphasise that the Pahang government has not appointed any individual, agent or company to handle the alienation of state government land outside the procedures stipulated by law.

items.title: Penang mulls holding Pesta Pulau Pinang in Seberang Perai this year
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — The Penang state government is considering organising the annual Pesta Pulau Pinang at Seberang Perai towards the end of this year. Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the cultural festival could be held on a smaller scale in North Seberang Perai. On the original Pesta site in Sungai Nibong, Chow said the draft Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) Master Plan covers about 23.47 hectares (58 acres).

items.title: Rohingya activist urges Asean to halt repatriation until Myanmar is safe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia has urged Asean member states, including Malaysia, not to repatriate Rohingya refugees until what it described as the "ongoing genocide" in Myanmar is resolved. "We have no citizenship, safety or dignity there," said Zafar, 56, president of the Myanmar Ethnic Rohingya Human Rights Organisation Malaysia. "The Rohingya refugees are not a burden.

items.title: Adibah Amin’s writings should be taught in schools to promote unity, says UM pro-chancellor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The works of acclaimed Malaysian journalist, writer and educator Adibah Amin should be incorporated into the school curriculum to instil the values of unity, tolerance and nationhood among younger generations, former Federal Court Judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali said. The Universiti Malaya Pro-Chancellor said Adibah’s writings remained highly relevant as Malaysia continued to navigate issues of race, religion and social cohesion. Adibah Amin’s As I Was Passing belongs squarely to the latter,” she said.

items.title: Kelantan authorities uncover ‘sympathy-selling’ tactic by snack sellers near ATMs, some earning up to RM300 a day
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, July 30 — Three Thai women selling snacks outside automated teller machines (ATMs) around the city are believed to have used a “sympathy-selling” tactic to gain public compassion and donations before they were rescued in an Integrated Op Mesra last night. Kelantan Social Welfare Department (JKM) director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said investigations found that the activity was not a genuine business, but rather a tactic to solicit contributions from people entering and leaving ATM areas. Che Samsuzuki said eight individuals were rescued, comprising three Thai women, three local men, one local woman aged between 48 and 70, and a nine-year-old boy.

items.title: Authorities dismiss Bangi escape rumour after four drug rehabilitation inmates rearrested in Perak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The National Anti-Drugs Agency (AADK) has confirmed that four inmates from the Perlop Narcotics Addiction Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) in Perak, who escaped on Friday (July 24), have been rearrested. AADK director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said all four were detained in the Sungai Siput district with the cooperation of the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) and local villagers. “The viral message is false as all four inmates escaped and remained within the Sungai Siput district before they were rearrested,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia belongs to all after apologising over remark that upset Indian community
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has reiterated his apology to the Indian community over his earlier use of a term which he acknowledged was inappropriate, admitting that he had chosen the wrong word while expressing his views. “The Prime Minister is only human. Also present were Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil, Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan, as well as leaders of non-governmental organisations (NGOs) and prominent members of the local Indian community.

items.title: Penang says DOSM tourism survey does not reflect full visitor numbers
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, July 30 — Penang’s tourism and creative economy committee chairman Wong Hon Wai today said the Department of Statistics Malaysia’s (DOSM) Domestic Tourism Survey 2025 should not be treated as a definitive measure of the state’s tourism performance as it was based on a sample survey. He said the survey also included day trippers and those travelling interstate to visit family members. Wong said actual hotel accommodation data provided a more reliable indicator of tourism performance.

items.title: Tabung Haji’s RM88b depositor guarantee could be triggered if LTH fails, says RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — The government’s guarantee to depositors of Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), currently worth RM88 billion, will be activated should TH fail to implement the LTH Recovery and Restructuring Plan 2018, according to the Tabung Haji Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). In the RCI Report investigating TH’s management and operational issues from 2014-2020 released yesterday, the RCI said that the government should give serious consideration to the implementation of TH’s recovery plan to ensure the pilgrimage board achieves its goals. In general, the RCI found that TH is exposed to strategic risks in the country’s financial ecosystem.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan palace revokes two titles awarded to Rais Yatim
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, has ordered the immediate revocation of the Darjah Seri Utama Negeri Sembilan (SPNS) and Darjah Dato’ Setia Negeri Sembilan (DSNS) awards conferred on Tan Sri Dr Mohd Rais Yatim. Negeri Sembilan Awards Registrar Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim said in a statement issued today that the decision was made to preserve the dignity, honour and prestige of the Negri Sembilan Royal Institution. “The Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan has ordered the revocation of the Darjah Seri Utama Negeri Sembilan (SPNS) (2001) and Darjah Dato’ Setia Negeri Sembilan (DSNS) (1979) awards conferred on Tan Sri Dr Mohd Rais Yatim, effective immediately,” he said.

items.title: Give Aminuddin another term to make state and Malaysia regional examples, Anwar tells Negeri Sembilan voters
items.summary: He said although the government still faced various challenges and unresolved issues, efforts would continue to improve governance for the well-being of the people. I want Negeri Sembilan and Malaysia to become examples for the region. “But we must continue working hard.

items.title: Report: MyIMMs hacking syndicate allegedly paid up to RM6,000 in bribes to immigration officers
items.summary: The Malay daily reported that according to a source, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained 12 individuals comprising two company directors, three foreigners, six JIM officers including two from the Information Technology Division, and a police officer, who are suspected of being involved in hacking the system. “Five male suspects have been remanded for three days until July 31 (Friday), while another five men and two women have been remanded for two days until July 30 (Thursday),” the source was quoted as saying. The source added that searches were conducted at company premises, as well as JIM Penang and the JIM headquarters in Putrajaya.

items.title: KL’s Mid Valley pipe bomb threat was a hoax, police confirm, now tracking sender of email
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Police have confirmed that the pipe bomb threat at Centrepoint South Tower, Mid Valley City here last night was a hoax, and that no explosives were found at the premises. Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the Brickfields district police headquarters (IPD) Control Centre received a call regarding the incident from the building’s security manager at 8.17 pm. “Acting on the information, the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) Bomb Disposal Unit and K9 Unit were deployed to conduct a thorough inspection of the premises at 10.30 pm.

items.title: RCI finds Tabung Haji’s 2017 profit should have been a RM1.4b loss
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) should have posted a net loss of RM1.4 billion in the 2017 financial year, instead of the RM3.4 billion profit reported in its financial statements, according to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The RCI report published tonight found that had the Malaysian Financial Reporting Standards (MFRS) been fully applied for the 2017 financial year, TH would have recorded a net loss, indicating that the institution’s financial position was already critical at the time. The report also stated that TH had distributed profits (hibah) for the 2017 financial year without taking into account the impact of impairment and declines in the fair value of investments, while also recording dividend income from subsidiaries despite the dividends not being paid to TH.

items.title: Asyraf Wajdi questions timing of Tabung Haji issue during Negri Sembilan polls
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, July 30 — Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki has questioned why issues involving Tabung Haji were raised during the Negri Sembilan state election campaign, although he welcomed efforts to bring the matter to public attention, Sinar Harian reported. Asyraf said calls for a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) to investigate allegations involving Tabung Haji had actually been made six years ago when he was leading the Umno Youth wing. He said this to reporters after the Community Chinese Gathering Programme in Kampung Pachitan, Chuah here yesterday.

items.title: RCI wants forensic audit into 14 Tabung Haji investments
items.summary: The RCI, which investigated TH’s management issues between 2014 and 2020, identified the investments requiring further scrutiny in a report released today. The 14 investments identified for forensic audit were PT TH Indo Plantations; Emrail Sdn Bhd; Wellspring Worldwide Ltd; Deru Semangat Sdn Bhd; Trurich Resources Sdn Bhd; Abraj Sdn Bhd; Putrajaya Perdana Bhd; Al-Rawda Real Estates Development & Project Management Co Ltd; Alfareeda Residential Fund; TH Plantations Bhd; TH Properties Sdn Bhd; Alam Maritim Resources/TH Marine; TH Hotel & Residences Sdn Bhd; and FGV Bhd. The RCI also stressed that TH’s investment functions, including investment management and profit distribution, must be carried out independently and professionally.

items.title: Tabung Haji RCI report reveals political interference in pilgrim fund’s management
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, July 30 — Weak governance, including political interference in the management of Tabung Haji (TH) and the distribution of its profits, was among the key findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into the pilgrim fund’s operations from 2014 to 2020. The RCI report, released tonight, found that political involvement in TH’s management between 2014 and 2018 had fuelled public concern amid political rivalry. The RCI also recommended that the Investment Panel, Syariah Advisory Committee and Haj Management Committee be expressly provided for under Act 535 to further strengthen TH’s governance.

items.title: DAP's Anthony Loke accuses rivals of smear campaign during Negeri Sembilan polls
items.summary: JELEBU, July 30 — DAP secretary-general Loke Siew Fook has accused his political opponents of mounting a smear campaign against him during the Negri Sembilan election campaign, including claims that he would be appointed menteri besar if Pakatan Harapan (PH) wins, according to a report by Free Malaysia Today (FMT). FMT reported that Loke, who is defending the Chennah seat for PH, said baseless claims had been spread in villages to frighten Malay voters, including allegations that Malays would lose their political power if the coalition won Saturday’s election. FMT reported that during the campaign, Umno secretary-general Datuk Seri Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki had questioned whether Loke would be nominated as PH’s menteri besar candidate if former menteri besar Aminuddin Harun lost in the state election, and whether the people would accept such a nomination.

items.title: Zahid says Tabung Haji RCI review should cover recovery period too
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — The Cabinet has proposed that the review period for the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) be extended to include the period of transition following the institution’s takeover by the new management. Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the move would allow the recovery measures undertaken after the investigation period to be assessed. Ahmad Zahid, who is also the Rural and Regional Development Minister, said the Cabinet had also agreed for the RCI Report to be made public and tabled at a special Parliament sitting for debate.

items.title: Anwar says special sitting needed for open debate on Tabung Haji report
items.summary: SEREMBAN, July 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has proposed holding a special Parliament sitting to discuss the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) as soon as possible. He said the date, however, would need the approval of Dewan Rakyat speaker Tan Sri Dr Johari Abdul. He said the report would also be tabled and debated during a special Dewan Rakyat sitting soon.
